maudhui: (1) Unless he sooner resigns or dies, a person elected, or appointed in accordance with Article 37(5), as Vice-President shall hold office for a period of five years. (2) The Vice-President shall hold office until - (a) his term of office expires; (b) he dies while in office; (c) he resigns; (d) he takes the oath as President after the office of President becomes vacant; (e) he is convicted of a criminal offence involving dishonesty; (f) another President together with his Vice-President takes the oath of office; (g) he is removed from office following impeachment by the National Assembly; or (h) he otherwise ceases to hold the office of Vice-President. (3) The National Assembly shall have the same power to remove the Vice-President from office as it has in relation to the President, save that a motion to impeach the Vice-President may be moved only where it is alleged that - (a) the President has submitted a certificate to the Speaker; (b) he has committed acts which violate the Constitution; (c) he has contravened the code of ethics concerning political parties; or (d) he has conducted himself in a manner that lowers the esteem of the office. (4) Where the office of Vice-President becomes vacant by reason of the provisions of subarticle (3), death or resignation, the President shall as soon as possible, and in any event within fourteen days, appoint a person to be Vice-President and such appointment shall be confirmed by the National Assembly by a majority vote of the Members of Parliament. (5) The other provisions of Article 46A shall apply in relation to the Vice-President, except that a Vice-President who is removed from office under subarticle (3) shall not be qualified to hold the office of President, Vice-President, Prime Minister or President of Zanzibar.
